headline: The first day.
intro: Frau Weber’s very first German lesson in Berlin. Frau Weber welcomes him — and the first thing he learns is how to spell his own name, letter by letter, and where those two little dots come from.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: der, die, das.
intro: Kai points around the classroom and Julia names each object — but every noun comes with a colour: der, die or das. A quick trick turns the hardest habit in German into a game.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: No, thanks.
intro: Lunchtime talk. Ben has no time, Anna has no more money, and the two learn the two ways to say no in German — kein for things, nicht for everything else.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: In the shop.
intro: Tom and Lisa go shopping after class. Tom is looking for a few things — and every object he wants becomes a direct object in the accusative.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: How is it really?
intro: Marie asks Leon to describe his city and his friends. With sein and an adjective, Leon paints a picture of his new life in Berlin.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Hanna is working at a café in Berlin when Simon comes in for breakfast — and the food words arrive before any rule does.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: After class, Ida drops into a café in Kreuzberg. The waiter takes her order, the prices come up, and she settles the bill — every café phrase you need, in one real scene.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: It is Friday after class. Elias asks Sara about the weekend, and their hobbies come out — Sara\u2019s tennis, Elias\u2019s photography, and one firm preference for the sofa.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Jan signs up for the Goethe exam. Frau Roth helps him fill out the registration form line by line — family name, address, postcode, email — so every piece of personal info from Chapters 1\u201316 gets one more workout.
objective: See how this checkpoint pulls Chapters 1\u201316 together.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: A normal morning at the Uni. Nora and Nora sort out how they get there, where they eat, who sees the library, and whether there\u2019s cake in the Mensa — and almost every verb in the scene is an irregular one changing its stem.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Pia asks Pia about his daily routine, and Pia chimes in with his (not very disciplined) version. As they compare mornings, noons and nights, the verb keeps landing in the same place — position 2 — no matter what word starts the sentence.
objective: See the one rule that controls every German main clause.

headline: Say it again.
intro: Second lesson, pure sound. Frau Bauer coaches Jonas through the five German vowels and the umlauts that Hindi does not have — and Jonas finds his inner German.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: A party is coming. Jule wants to plan it, Jule definitely wants to come, and Jule must finish his homework first. As they sort out who can do what, every sentence shows the same shape — modal in position 2, main verb at the very end.
objective: See the one structure behind every modal-verb sentence.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: After the party plan, the group needs a time. Mara checks the calendar, Mara has class until the afternoon, and Mara — predictably — wants the latest possible start. Watch how every appointment locks onto the clock with um, am and von … bis.
objective: See the two clock styles and the one trap (halb acht = 7:30).

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Career day comes up in the canteen. Lea wants to be a doctor, Lea has just landed an internship, and Lea\u2014between naps\u2014finally admits what he actually wants to do. Watch the two job patterns appear again and again: Ich bin … and Ich arbeite als …
objective: See the two job patterns before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Ines brings a family photo to the canteen. As Ines and Ines pass it around, every "this is my…/her…/his…" puts a possessive article to work — and Ines, of course, has a photo of someone unexpected.
objective: See the one rule behind every possessive article.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Katja\u2019s birthday is coming. The group plans a surprise party around the calendar \u2014 fixing the date, counting the guests, and sorting out gifts \u2014 so ordinal numbers and months come up in every line.
objective: See how ordinals and the date phrase work before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Saturday morning. Svenja calls Svenja to plan the day \u2014 getting up, shopping, picking up Svenja \u2014 and almost every plan is a separable verb whose prefix lands, with a little click, at the end of the sentence.
objective: See how a separable verb splits before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: The study group agreed to meet at four to prepare for the checkpoint. It\u2019s ten past \u2014 and Britta is missing again. When he finally arrives, the lesson becomes a real one: how to apologise, accept an apology, and arrange the next appointment, German-style.
objective: See how this checkpoint pulls Chapters 1\u201325 together.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Monday morning. Doris missed the weekend get-together, so Doris and Doris fill him in on what happened — where everyone was, who had cake, and why Doris\u2019s day was, as usual, a small disaster. Every sentence lands in the past with war and hatte.
objective: See why war and hatte are your whole past tense for now.
